text:
Maria: heads-up — p99 for /v1/generate spiked from ~120ms to ~420ms around 10:11 UTC; p50/p95 unchanged. Route-level p99 shows ~180ms.

Josh: could be a routing/quota fallback. paste the console query you ran?

Maria: ran this:```SELECT percentile(response_ms, [50,95,99]) FROM latency WHERE endpoint='/v1/generate' AND timestamp >= '2024-05-05T10:05:00Z' AND timestamp <= '2024-05-05T10:20:00Z' GROUP BY route, sample_source```

Kevin: FYI sample_source = gateway | cache_hit | backend. Our rollup contract historically drops sample_source when merging route rollups, so route p99 is aggregated from mixed-origin t-digests while endpoint p99 is often recomputed from backend histograms after KV-cache filtering. That divergence explains different tails.

Maria: endpoint/backend view shows p99 ~430ms; route view ~180ms. Why would backend-only show such a tail but not route?

Liz: gateway + cache_hit dominate numerically with low latency. Route rollup is overwhelmed by those. Backend has few samples but a heavy tail — masked in the mixed rollup.

Maria: can we get counts for 10:05–10:20 by origin?

Kevin: quick query gave: gateway: 1,200; cache_hit: 1,020; backend: 80. backend N is tiny.

Maria: that nails it. Proposal: surface per-percentile effective-N and show confidence badge when effective-N < 100 (avoid noisy alerts). Also annotate percentiles with sample_origin.

Liz: UX idea: small badge next to each percentile e.g. "p99 (origin: backend)" or "p99 (mixed)". Hover shows breakdown and effective N by origin. Red ⚠ low-N marker if N < 100. Clicking expands raw sample distribution.

Josh: sounds actionable. I9ll file a tracking ticket with Maria's repro and Kevin's counts. Runbook note for ops: "If route p99 != endpoint p99, verify sample_origin counts and effective-N before paging SRE." Tagging eng-platform and oncall.

incident-bot: quota-fallback triggered client=acme-corp at 2024-05-05T10:11:07Z — routing policy switched client keys to fallback-model-v2.

Kevin: another factor: recent batching change batches short requests aggressively at gateway (reduces observed tail there). Long-sequence requests often bypass batching and show up in backend tail. Suggest adding sequence-length stratifier to latency pane.

Maria: repro steps I ran locally: 1) POST /v1/generate with ~2000 tokens and header `x-client: dedicated-client`; 2) observed backend p99 ~420ms. log: `req_id=... backend_ms=420 seq_len=2000 cache=false`.

Liz: I mocked a tiny tooltip/ badge in the console frontend — minimal copy: "Percentiles are calculated per sample origin. Differences between endpoint and route views can come from sampling, KV-cache filtering, and rollup behavior. Hover to see per-origin counts and effective sample size (N)."

Kevin: I'll add a short metric `percentile_effective_n` in the next infra deploy so console can ingest it.

Josh: good. I'll also update dashboard docs/FAQ and close the loop once PR lands.

Maria: thanks — tagging @eng-platform for visibility. :eyes:
